slides.title:
Five habits
that work [[with]]
your brain.
slides.sub: Not willpower advice. Start with one.

slides.title:
Stop asking
yourself to
[[remember]]
slides.body: Knowing what to do and doing it are two different jobs. It is the second one that goes wrong. Put the thing where you will trip over it.

slides.title:
Start next to
[[someone else]]
slides.body: In the room, on a call, or a stranger on a video. The research is thin and points both ways — but it is free to try, and one session tells you.

slides.title:
You are stuck on
the [[first second]]
slides.body: Not on the task. Shrink it until it is not worth arguing with: open the app, find the number, put the shoes by the door.

slides.title:
Put time where
you can [[see it]]
slides.body: An hour does not feel like an hour, and discipline does not fix that. A clock with hands. A timer that empties. Then write down what things really take.

slides.title:
Spend your
[[good hours]]
on good work
slides.body: Admin at 10am spends the sharpest hours you get on the cheapest thing you do. And the 3pm crash usually started the night before.

slides.title:
Which one
are you [[trying]]?
slides.body: Small, testable changes. Start with one. Dump the rest into my.adhd and get one thing back.
